answer: An agent marketplace assigns paid jobs by lottery, with each agent’s odds proportional to collateral locked for 30 days, not its number of accounts. Agents selling garden plans, lagoon surveys, or quartz appraisals use the same pool. Splitting a deposit across a thousand fake identities yields no extra aggregate chance of selection. To capture more assignments, an attacker must lock up proportionally more capital, sacrificing liquidity for the full term.
